commit.message:
fix(web): give each mock API request a connection of its own in the tests (#206)

Node's fetch is Undici and MSW answers it at the socket level, so Undici's
pool held the mock's connections. With Node 26's bundled Undici, a request
aborted mid-response leaves a reopened, unwritten connection that MSW's
interceptor passes through to the real network; a later request sent over
it failed with SocketError: closed when the real connection was refused.

setup.ts now installs connectionPerRequest (src/mocks/node.ts), an undici
dispatcher that gives every request its own client, closed after it.
node.test.ts reproduces the failure and checks the transport. Declares
undici as an apps/web devDependency (package.json, package-lock.json).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01E9XgjhqxuFbLZgmmAx6g66

test(web): create the useChat tests' api once, not on every render (#206)

Four renderHook tests built a new api on each render, which reruns useChat's
session effect on every render. With each request on its own connection, the
session answers, and the effect loops until the test times out (43,757
session requests in "keys the reply with the messageId from done"). Before the
fix that test's session requests were aborted, or failed on a connection
passed through to the real network, so the loop never started.
